video:video.video:title: ISB DLabs I-HEAL Fourth Cohort: 15 Health Startups Building AI-Led Solutions for India's Most Overlo
video:video.video:description: The Indian School of Business's DLabs accelerator has unveiled 15 startups in the fourth cohort of its I-HEAL healthcare programme, each targeting persistent and underserved gaps across India's health system — from diagnostics and rehabilitation to hearing health, which affects over 63 million Indians. The cohort reflects a broader push to build technology-enabled solutions that can reach patients beyond urban hospital infrastructure. Several startups are deploying AI for early diagnosis, remote monitoring, and personalised care pathways in areas where specialist access is limited. The programme positions ISB as a key institutional bridge between academic research and applied health innovation in India.

video:video.video:title: MeitY's Section 69A Blocked Anti-Gambling App Gamban for Three Years Without Disclosing Reasons
video:video.video:description: UK-based Gamban, an app designed to help people block access to gambling sites and protect themselves from addiction, says India's Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology blocked it under Section 69A of the IT Act for three years without providing any reasons or formal order. MeitY has cited privacy concerns as a justification, but Gamban's representatives describe the block as arbitrary and legally unfounded, noting the irony of a harm-reduction tool being censored without explanation. The case spotlights how opaque India's content blocking regime can be, even when the affected party is a consumer protection service. It adds a concrete new example to ongoing debates about the accountability and proportionality of Section 69A orders.

video:video.video:title: Skyroot's Vikram-1 — India's First Private Orbital Rocket — Set for Launch From Sriharikota Within W
video:video.video:description: Hyderabad-based Skyroot Aerospace is weeks away from launching Vikram-1, which would become India's first privately developed orbital rocket to reach space, lifting off from ISRO's Sriharikota launch facility. The test flight will carry diverse payloads and is designed primarily to gather engineering data that will underpin future commercial missions. A successful launch would establish Skyroot as a credible competitor for global satellite launch contracts, building on India's reputation as a cost-effective launch destination. The milestone reflects the maturation of India's private space sector following policy reforms that opened ISRO's infrastructure to commercial operators.

video:video.video:title: Independent Media and Online Critics Face Growing Censorship Risk as India's Content Takedown Infras
video:video.video:description: An investigative report by The Hindu finds that an expanding infrastructure of content takedown mechanisms — enabled by existing laws and IT rules — is being used by Central and State governments to suppress social media content, with independent media outlets and online critics increasingly caught in its crosshairs. The report documents how, in an environment of heightened concern about misinformation and deepfakes, legitimate opposing voices are also being targeted under the same regulatory tools. The analysis highlights how the lack of transparency in takedown orders makes it nearly impossible for affected parties to challenge removals. The piece adds fresh evidence to ongoing expert concerns about the erosion of digital free speech in India.

video:video.video:title: Apple Calls India's Competition Commission an Overreach as CCI-Apple Antitrust Dispute Intensifies
video:video.video:description: Apple has formally accused India's Competition Commission (CCI) of overstepping its judicial authority after the regulator sought detailed financial information from the company — data typically requested when calculating penalties — following a 2024 investigation that found Apple abused its dominant position in the Indian app marketplace. Apple has disputed the CCI's jurisdiction to compel such disclosures, escalating what began as a regulatory inquiry into a high-stakes legal confrontation. The dispute has significant implications for how India regulates Big Tech, particularly as the government attempts to assert stronger sovereign oversight over dominant platform ecosystems. The outcome could set a precedent for how foreign tech giants respond to Indian antitrust authority.

video:video.video:title: IndiaMART Stops Reporting Traffic Metrics as AI Agent Bots Overwhelm Platform With Agentic Traffic
video:video.video:description: IndiaMART, India's largest B2B e-commerce marketplace, has quietly stopped disclosing its 'unique business inquiries' traffic metric after agentic AI bots began flooding the platform with automated queries, distorting data that investors and sellers had relied on to gauge platform health. The company introduced OTP verification to filter bot traffic, but this created a 1% drop in genuine user conversion in Q4 FY26, illustrating the trade-off between data integrity and user friction. The shift marks a significant moment for Indian digital commerce: AI agents are now active enough to meaningfully disrupt the reporting and operations of a major public platform. This is one of the first documented cases of an Indian company formally abandoning a key business metric due to AI agent interference.

video:video.video:title: Tata Electronics Targets $30 Billion Revenue With India's First Semiconductor Fab and Global Custome
video:video.video:description: Tata Electronics CEO and MD Randhir Thakur says the company aims to become a $30 billion business within five years, anchored by India's first semiconductor fabrication plant and an assembly and test unit currently under construction. The company has already achieved significant revenue growth and crossed into profitability, while securing global customers and manufacturing partnerships. Tata Electronics is simultaneously scaling its iPhone component manufacturing operations, making it one of India's most strategically significant industrial plays in electronics and semiconductors. The ambition positions India as a genuine alternative to China in global chip supply chains.

video:video.video:title: UpGrad to Acquire Unacademy for Rs 2,055 Crore — 90% Below Peak Valuation in India's Edtech Reckonin
video:video.video:description: Ronnie Screwvala's UpGrad is set to acquire Unacademy for approximately Rs 2,055 crore — a valuation nearly 90% below Unacademy's peak of over Rs 20,000 crore — marking one of the starkest corrections in India's edtech sector since its pandemic-era peak. The deal, which follows months of on-again, off-again negotiations, is being financed partly through an internal fundraising round of approximately Rs 375 crore from existing backers including Temasek, a common investor in both companies. The consolidation reflects broader pressure on India's online learning platforms as post-COVID enrolment normalised and profitability proved elusive. The combined entity would position UpGrad as India's dominant working-professional upskilling platform.

video:video.video:title: India's Major IT Firms Record Rising Revenue Per Employee as AI and Automation Drive Productivity Sh
video:video.video:description: India's top IT companies — including TCS, Infosys, HCLTech, and Tech Mahindra — have reported measurable increases in revenue generated per employee, a metric that signals a structural shift away from the traditional headcount-driven business model. Analysts attribute the gains to widespread adoption of AI coding assistants, automation of routine service tasks, and leaner project delivery pipelines. The trend suggests firms are extracting more value from existing workforces rather than scaling headcount proportionally with revenue. This marks one of the clearest financial confirmations yet that AI-led productivity is reshaping how India's $250-billion IT industry operates.

video:video.video:title: GalaxEye Launches World's First OptoSAR Satellite — India's Largest Private Space Payload Reaches Or
video:video.video:description: Indian deep-tech startup GalaxEye successfully launched Mission Drishti aboard a SpaceX rocket, making it the world's first satellite to combine electro-optical and synthetic aperture radar (OptoSAR) sensors in a single 190-kilogram platform — the largest satellite ever built by an Indian private company. The satellite is designed to capture high-quality Earth observation data regardless of weather or lighting conditions, overcoming limitations of conventional single-sensor systems. Prime Minister Narendra Modi publicly hailed the launch as a landmark achievement for India's private space sector. GalaxEye expects to begin commercial data sales within eight weeks, with defence and security agencies anticipated as anchor customers.

video:video.video:title: MobiKwik Secures NBFC Licence From RBI, Launches Own Lending Subsidiary to Move Beyond Distribution
video:video.video:description: Digital payments and financial services platform MobiKwik has received a Non-Banking Financial Company licence from the Reserve Bank of India, allowing it to launch its own lending subsidiary, MobiKwik Financial Services Private Limited, and move from being a lending distributor to a direct lender. The NBFC licence is a significant regulatory milestone that gives MobiKwik control over its own credit products, pricing, and underwriting rather than acting as a pass-through for partner NBFCs. This transition is expected to improve unit economics and enable the platform to offer more competitive loan products to its user base of tens of millions of Indians.

video:video.video:title: Snabbit Raises $56M in Six Months After Last Round as Instant Home Services Race Intensifies in Indi
video:video.video:description: On-demand home services startup Snabbit has raised $56 million in a new round co-led by Susquehanna Venture Capital, Mirae Asset Venture Investments, and Bertelsmann India Investments, bringing its total capital raised to $112 million in under a year. The rapid successive fundraising reflects intensifying investor interest in India's instant home services category, where Snabbit competes to connect urban households with vetted domestic help on short notice. The company plans to use the capital to expand city coverage and deepen its service category range.

video:video.video:title: HyugaLife Raises Rs 100 Crore Series A to Scale AI Personalisation and Dark Store Network Across Ind
video:video.video:description: Health and wellness e-commerce platform HyugaLife has closed a Rs 100 crore Series A round led by IvyCap Ventures, which it will deploy to strengthen its AI-driven personalisation engine, expand its dark store fulfilment network, and open offline retail touchpoints. The company uses AI to match customers with personalised health product recommendations based on lifestyle data, aiming to compete in India's rapidly growing wellness commerce segment. The funding positions HyugaLife to scale beyond its current urban customer base into Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets.

video:video.video:title: Magellanic Cloud and Rayonix Tech Form Rs 100-Crore JV With Israel's Xtend to Make Drones in India
video:video.video:description: Indian technology firms Magellanic Cloud and Rayonix Tech have announced a Rs 100-crore joint venture with Israeli drone technology company Xtend to manufacture advanced unmanned aerial vehicles in India. The JV aims to meet India's growing demand for sophisticated drones, with the first production-ready drone sets expected within four to six months. The initiative aligns with India's Make in India push for defence and dual-use technology self-reliance, reducing dependence on imported UAV systems.

video:video.video:title: Sahamati Raises Rs 50 Crore to Deepen India's Account Aggregator Ecosystem
video:video.video:description: Sahamati, the industry alliance backing India's Account Aggregator financial data-sharing framework, has raised Rs 50 crore from financial sector entities to strengthen its technical and policy infrastructure. The capital will be used to deepen ecosystem participation among banks, insurers, and fintech players who use the AA framework to enable consent-based financial data sharing for millions of Indians. The Account Aggregator system is a foundational piece of India's Digital Public Infrastructure and underpins credit access for underserved borrowers.

video:video.video:title: Paytring Uses OpenAI Models to Fix Payment Chaos for Indian Merchants — Founder Explains How
video:video.video:description: Bengaluru-based fintech startup Paytring has built a payment orchestration layer for Indian merchants that uses OpenAI's language models to improve transaction success rates and simplify checkout operations. Founder Debal Chakraborty explains that AI is used to route payments intelligently across multiple gateways, reducing failures that cost merchants revenue on every failed transaction. The startup addresses a gap in India's booming digital payments ecosystem where checkout friction remains a persistent problem for small and mid-sized businesses.

video:video.video:title: India's Content Takedown Rules Under Scrutiny: Experts Warn of Expanding Powers With No Transparency
video:video.video:description: A MediaNama discussion surfaced expert warnings that India's content-blocking legal framework is being expanded through draft IT Rules in ways that are largely hidden from public view, with experts saying what is not disclosed may be more consequential than what is. Former MeitY official Rakesh Maheshwari and former Meta public policy manager Snehashish Ghosh traced the origins of the three-hour content takedown mandate to the 2019 election code of ethics, revealing how an emergency electoral measure has been normalised into permanent regulatory architecture. Panellists warned that the lack of transparency in how blocking decisions are made leaves citizens and platforms with no meaningful redress.

video:video.video:title: India's Draft IT Rules Trigger Free Speech Fears as IDC Gains Powers to Block Online Content
video:video.video:description: The Hindu's editorial analysis of India's proposed IT Rules amendments warns that the draft departs from existing Supreme Court rulings and consolidates content-blocking authority in the executive, raising the risk of digital overreach. The piece highlights how the proposed Inter-Departmental Committee structure lacks judicial checks, giving bureaucrats power to restrict online speech without transparency or appeal mechanisms. Legal experts cited in the article argue the rules conflict with constitutional free speech protections.

video:video.video:title: Experts Warn MeitY's Draft IT Rules Give Executive Power to Issue Binding AI Advisories, Bypassing P
video:video.video:description: Legal and policy experts at a MediaNama event raised serious alarms over proposed Rule 3(4) in India's draft IT Rules amendments, which they say allows MeitY to issue binding advisories, guidelines, and standard operating procedures without parliamentary oversight or judicial review. Critics argue the provision effectively hands the executive branch unchecked authority to shape what speech is permissible online, with no mandatory transparency mechanism. The concern is compounded by separate warnings about an Inter-Departmental Committee being granted expansive powers to act as 'judge, jury, and executioner' over online content.

video:video.video:title: MeitY Secretary Confirms India in Direct Talks With Anthropic Over Mythos Cybersecurity Threat
video:video.video:description: India's Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology Secretary S. Krishnan confirmed the Union government is in direct talks with Anthropic regarding concerns over the Mythos AI model, describing AI's impact on cybersecurity as a 'very real threat' that has materialised 'in very real terms.' The development signals the Indian government's escalating concern about advanced AI capabilities posing risks to national digital infrastructure. This is the first confirmed high-level bilateral engagement between MeitY and Anthropic specifically on the Mythos vulnerability.

video:video.video:title: Infosys Delays Salary Hike Decision Amid AI-Driven Cost Pressures and Cautious FY27 Revenue Outlook
video:video.video:description: Infosys management has told employees at a recent town hall that the company has not yet decided on salary revision timelines, citing macroeconomic uncertainty and cautious client spending — with communication already delayed by four months. The non-commitment comes as Infosys forecasts modest revenue growth for FY27 and faces compounding pressure from AI-driven productivity tools that are reducing billable headcount requirements. The development signals broader structural tension across India's IT sector, where AI efficiency gains are increasingly being absorbed as margin improvement rather than passed on to employees as wage growth.

video:video.video:title: IAMAI Alleges TRAI Is Overstepping to Regulate OTT Platforms Like WhatsApp Under Spam Call Rules
video:video.video:description: India's Internet and Mobile Association (IAMAI) has formally alleged that the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) is exceeding its jurisdiction by attempting to bring over-the-top platforms such as WhatsApp under the scope of proposed anti-spam regulations designed for traditional telecom services. IAMAI argues that OTT platforms are not telecommunications services and that requiring them to share user data under these rules would be unconstitutional. The dispute raises fundamental questions about regulatory boundaries in an era where AI-driven communication platforms increasingly blur the line between telecom and internet services.

video:video.video:title: Jamtara Is Old News: How AI-Powered Synthetic Identity Fraud Is Now Threatening India's Digital Lend
video:video.video:description: As India's digital lending sector scales rapidly, AI-powered synthetic identity fraud has emerged as a structural threat to the underwriting models that lenders rely upon, according to a YourStory analysis. Fraudsters are now using generative AI to construct convincing fake identities — combining real and fabricated personal data — that pass conventional KYC and credit scoring checks, forcing lenders to rethink risk assessment from the ground up. The piece argues that fraud is no longer a downstream compliance problem but has become an upstream design challenge embedded in how digital credit is originated in India.

video:video.video:title: Infosys Co-Founder Kris Gopalakrishnan: Deep Tech and Advanced Manufacturing Will Drive India's Unic
video:video.video:description: Infosys co-founder Kris Gopalakrishnan has called for India's next generation of startups to anchor themselves in deep technology and advanced manufacturing rather than software services, framing this pivot as essential for national self-reliance and long-term competitive advantage. Gopalakrishnan described this shift as 'Unicorn 2.0', arguing that proprietary technology — including AI — must underpin future high-value companies rather than imported platforms or service arbitrage. His remarks carry weight given Infosys's own AI-driven restructuring pressures and reflect a growing consensus among India's senior tech leadership about where sustainable value creation lies.

video:video.video:title: NITI Aayog Report: India's Digital Public Infrastructure Could Contribute 4% of GDP by 2030
video:video.video:description: A new NITI Aayog report titled 'DPI@2047 for Viksit Bharat' projects that India's Digital Public Infrastructure initiatives — including UPI, Aadhaar, and emerging AI-linked data layers — could contribute up to 4% of GDP by 2030, describing the current moment as a 'once-in-a-generation inflection point'. The report lays out a strategic roadmap for non-linear, inclusive socio-economic growth through DPI expansion and calls for deeper integration of AI into public service delivery. The findings are significant for Indian policymakers, as they provide an official economic rationale for accelerating AI-linked digital infrastructure investment.

video:video.video:title: Google Breaks Ground on AI Data Centre in Visakhapatnam as Part of $15B India Investment
video:video.video:description: Google has officially broken ground on its AI data centre in Visakhapatnam, marking a concrete construction milestone in its announced $15 billion, five-year commitment to build a gigawatt-scale AI ecosystem in India. The facility is expected to become a major node in Google's Asia-Pacific AI infrastructure, providing cloud compute capacity to Indian enterprises, government bodies, and research institutions. The groundbreaking follows a series of high-level government engagements and positions Andhra Pradesh as a central geography in India's AI infrastructure buildout.

video:video.video:title: India's Draft IT Rules Draw Criticism for Expanding Content Blocking Powers With No Transparency Saf
video:video.video:description: The Hindu's editorial analysis of India's draft amendments to the Information Technology Rules warns that proposed changes represent a significant tightening of state control over the digital public sphere, departing from existing judicial rulings on free expression. The draft rules would expand the government's ability to block online content — including AI-generated material — without adequate transparency requirements, due process, or independent review mechanisms. Legal experts cited in the piece argue that the amendments risk enabling digital overreach at a scale that could chill legitimate speech for millions of internet users in India.

video:video.video:title: China Blocks Meta's Acquisition of AI Firm Manus — and the Move Has Direct Implications for India
video:video.video:description: China's top economic planning body has blocked Meta's acquisition of AI startup Manus, asserting origin-country jurisdiction over the deal — a move that sets a significant precedent for how nations can claim regulatory authority over AI companies based on where the technology was developed, regardless of where the transaction occurs. MediaNama's analysis highlights that this decision has direct implications for India, which is building its own AI regulatory architecture and considering how to treat cross-border AI acquisitions involving Indian-origin technology. The ruling raises questions about whether India should establish similar sovereign controls over its emerging AI startup ecosystem.

video:video.video:title: Experts Warn MeitY's Draft IT Rules Would Let Executive Bypass Parliament to Issue Binding AI Adviso
video:video.video:description: Legal and policy experts at a MediaNama discussion have raised alarm over proposed Rule 3(4) in India's draft IT Rules amendments, which would empower MeitY to issue binding advisories, guidelines, and standard operating procedures without parliamentary or judicial oversight. Critics argue this provision concentrates unprecedented executive power over online speech and platform behaviour, including AI-generated content. The concern follows a broader pattern flagged at the same event, where experts described proposed governance structures — including an Inter-Departmental Committee — as placing the government in the role of 'judge, jury, and executioner' over digital expression.

video:video.video:title: MeitY Secretary Confirms India in Direct Talks With Anthropic Over Mythos Cybersecurity Threat
video:video.video:description: India's Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) Secretary S. Krishnan has confirmed that the Union government is in direct dialogue with Anthropic over concerns raised by the release of its Mythos AI model. Krishnan described the cybersecurity impact of the model as a 'very real threat' that has materialised 'in very real terms'. The disclosure marks the first official Indian government acknowledgment of Mythos as an active national security concern, elevating the conversation beyond industry speculation to formal diplomatic and regulatory engagement.

video:video.video:title: RateGain Wins ET Emerging Company Award as AI-Powered Travel Intelligence Platform Scales Globally
video:video.video:description: Noida-based RateGain Travel Technologies has won the Economic Times Emerging Company of the Year award, recognised for its AI-driven platform that aggregates and analyses real-time data from over 1,100 sources to serve the global travel and hospitality industry. The company demonstrated strong post-pandemic revenue growth, maintained high client retention, and scaled rapidly to become one of India's leading B2B AI platforms for travel. RateGain's success illustrates how Indian AI startups can build globally competitive, specialised intelligence products.

video:video.video:title: HCL-Foxconn JV Picks Taiwanese Firm CTCI as EPC Partner for UP Semiconductor Plant Worth Rs 3,706 Cr
video:video.video:description: The HCL-Foxconn joint venture has appointed Taiwanese engineering firm CTCI as its engineering, procurement, and construction partner for a Rs 3,706 crore semiconductor assembly and testing facility in Uttar Pradesh. The OSAT plant will manufacture display driver chips and marks CTCI's first entry into India's semiconductor ecosystem. The appointment advances India's ambition to build a domestic semiconductor supply chain and reduces reliance on chip imports.

video:video.video:title: LTIMindtree CEO Says AI-Driven Cost Pressures Are Normal, Restructures Into Three Lines Including Ne
video:video.video:description: LTIMindtree CEO Venu Lambu has publicly downplayed concerns about AI-led revenue deflation, framing current pricing pressures as a natural phase of market evolution that requires adaptation rather than alarm. The company is reorganising its service structure into three lines, with a newly created Business AI unit designed to capture emerging demand for enterprise AI services. Lambu identified execution as the central challenge for Indian IT firms navigating this generational shift in technology.

video:video.video:title: India's Top 5 IT Firms Face Tepid FY27 Growth as AI Pricing Pressure Compounds Geopolitical Headwind
video:video.video:description: India's five largest IT services companies are forecasting modest revenue growth in FY27, squeezed between reduced client spending caused by geopolitical uncertainty and AI-driven price deflation in traditional IT services. While companies are maintaining stable margins through cost management, analysts warn that the benefits of new AI service lines have yet to materialise at scale. The subdued outlook has direct implications for hiring, salary growth, and the career trajectories of millions of Indian IT professionals.

video:video.video:title: Indian E-Commerce Giants Flipkart and Bigbasket Build AI Storefronts to Enable Autonomous Shopping
video:video.video:description: Indian e-commerce majors Flipkart and Bigbasket are actively building AI-powered storefronts that enable agentic commerce, where AI agents can autonomously search for, order, and pay for products on behalf of users through platforms like ChatGPT. Indian fintechs have already built the payment rails required for this automated transaction model, and quick commerce and travel are identified as the leading sectors for early adoption. The shift represents a fundamental change in how Indian consumers may interact with online retail within the next few years.

video:video.video:title: AI Helped Improve Water Resilience and Community Development in Rajasthan's Last-Mile Villages
video:video.video:description: A community development project in two Rajasthan districts used a lightweight AI application to strengthen water resilience and improve last-mile responsiveness among frontline government workers. The AI tool was designed to sit within existing large government programmes, enhancing local coordination and behaviour change without requiring heavy infrastructure. The project demonstrated that AI does not need to be large-scale or expensive to deliver meaningful impact in rural India.

video:video.video:title: India's Tele-MANAS Mental Health Helpline Reports Surge in Users Switching From AI to Human Counsell
video:video.video:description: India's government-run Tele-MANAS mental health helpline is recording a notable rise in callers who initially interact with its AI interface but then request to be transferred to a human counsellor, indicating that AI falls short in delivering adequate mental health support. The trend raises important questions about the deployment of AI in sensitive healthcare settings where empathy and contextual understanding are critical. Tele-MANAS, launched by the Union Ministry of Health, was designed to expand mental health access across India using a tiered AI-plus-human model.

video:video.video:title: MeitY Tightens AI Labelling Rules for India, Mandates Continuous Disclosure of AI-Generated Content
video:video.video:description: India's Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has issued updated regulations requiring platforms to apply continuous disclosure labels to AI-generated content, going beyond one-time labelling at upload. The new rules tighten accountability for platforms hosting synthetic media and are part of India's broader push to regulate AI outputs in public-facing digital spaces. This move follows growing global concern around AI-generated misinformation and deepfakes circulating on Indian social media platforms.

video:video.video:title: NASSCOM Chair: AI Will Accelerate India's Tech Industry, Not Replace Its Workforce
video:video.video:description: Newly appointed NASSCOM Chairman Srikanth Velamakanni has stated publicly that AI will act as an accelerator for India's technology sector rather than a threat to employment, affirming that the tech industry will continue hiring people. His remarks come at a critical juncture as India's IT sector faces twin pressures of geopolitical uncertainty and rapid AI-driven disruption. NASSCOM represents hundreds of Indian IT firms employing millions of workers, giving this leadership position significant weight in shaping industry and government narratives around AI and jobs.

video:video.video:title: Google's $15B AI Data Centre in Visakhapatnam to Make India a Premier AI Hub in Asia
video:video.video:description: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu will officially unveil Google's $15 billion AI data centre project in Visakhapatnam on April 28, 2026. The facility will carry a capacity of 1 gigawatt, one of the largest single AI infrastructure investments ever announced in Asia. The project is positioned to transform Visakhapatnam into a technology and AI hub with significant implications for jobs, digital infrastructure, and India's standing in the global AI race.

video:video.video:title: India Bets $277 Billion on AI Infrastructure — The Summit That Made India the World's AI Landlord
video:video.video:description: Companies gathered at the India AI Impact Summit collectively committed $277 billion in AI investment over five to seven years — the majority directed at building data centers, GPU clusters, and AI factories on Indian soil. Beyond the summit, the picture is already moving: Blackstone made a $600 million equity investment in Indian AI cloud startup Neysa, which plans to deploy over 20,000 GPUs. India's sovereign AI cloud capacity is on track to reach 100,000 GPUs by the end of 2026. The logic is strategic: every country that builds its AI on foreign clouds is a tenant. India is choosing to become the landlord — building infrastructure it owns, controls, and can rent to the rest of the Global South.

video:video.video:title: Krutrim's Bhashik Brings AI Voice Intelligence to 22 Indian Languages — Targets 500 Million Non-Engl
video:video.video:description: Krutrim, India's first AI unicorn backed by Ola founder Bhavish Aggarwal, has deployed Bhashik — a natively multilingual AI product targeting the 500 million Indians who conduct their daily lives entirely in regional languages. Krutrim-2, the underlying model trained on over 2 trillion tokens, supports 22 Indian languages with a 128K context window and powers Bhashik's vernacular speech products and Document Intelligence Service for enterprise document processing in local languages. The strategic bet is straightforward: the next billion AI users will not use AI in English. The company that owns native-language AI for India owns the largest untapped AI market in the world.

video:video.video:title: India's AI Hiring Moves to Skills-First — 2 Million Already Upskilled, Tier 2 Cities Surge
video:video.video:description: India's hiring market is undergoing a structural shift in 2026: employers are moving from degree-first to skills-first, and AI fluency — the ability to use AI to deliver results that once took a team of three — is now the primary filter. Over 2 million Indian professionals have already completed formal AI upskilling. Demand for generative AI and LLM skills surged nearly 60 percent year-on-year. The geographic story is equally significant: while Bengaluru leads with 26 percent of AI roles, Jaipur, Indore, and Mysuru are emerging as genuine AI job hubs, not just Tier 1 overflow. For a fresh graduate in a Tier 2 city, the window to enter a high-demand field with a skills certificate — not a postgraduate degree — has never been more open.

video:video.video:title: India's IndiaAI Innovation Challenge 2026 Opens — Ministry of AYUSH and MSME Back First Two Problems
video:video.video:description: IndiaAI has launched its Innovation Challenge 2026 — a competitive programme inviting startups and developers to submit market-deployed AI solutions that address real government problem statements. The first two partner ministries are the Ministry of AYUSH and the Ministry of MSME, targeting AI applications in traditional medicine, small business operations, and rural enterprise. Winners get pilots within government systems, not just prize money — a direct route from startup to national-scale deployment. This is India's version of using government as a customer and launchpad for AI companies that cannot afford the traditional enterprise sales cycle. For India's 63 million small businesses, AI tailored to their specific constraints and languages could be genuinely transformative.

video:video.video:title: Fractal Analytics Launches Vaidya 2.0 — India's Healthcare AI That Answers Symptoms in 22 Languages
video:video.video:description: Fractal Analytics has released Vaidya 2.0, a specialised healthcare AI model that allows patients in India to describe symptoms in any of 22 regional languages and receive safe, structured health guidance. The model is designed for deployment in primary health centres, ASHA worker programs, and rural telemedicine networks where doctors are scarce. India's AI healthcare market is projected to grow from $1.6 billion in 2025 to $34 billion by 2034, and the government has established three AI Centres of Excellence specifically for healthcare, agriculture, and sustainable cities. For a patient in rural Bihar or northeastern India who has never had easy access to a doctor, a multilingual AI health assistant is not a luxury — it is a first-responder.

video:video.video:title: RBI: Generative AI Could Boost Indian Banking Efficiency by 46% — 90% of Banks Already Using It
video:video.video:description: The Reserve Bank of India has reported that generative AI could boost banking efficiency by up to 46 percent, with applications spanning compliance, fraud detection, credit scoring, and customer service. Nearly 90 percent of Indian banks, fintechs, and insurers have now integrated AI into their strategic plans, and 60 to 70 percent are actively using it in live operations. An April 2026 regulatory deadline is also in effect: every digital transaction must now include an additional authentication layer beyond OTP — a change that will push banks to deploy smarter, faster AI-based verification systems. India already leads the world in real-time payments. In 2026, the goal is to lead in intelligent payments where AI, biometric identity, and global interoperability converge.

video:video.video:title: 91 Nations Sign India's New Delhi AI Declaration — Delhi Reframes Global AI From Risk to Impact
video:video.video:description: India hosted the global India AI Impact Summit 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, with delegations from over 100 countries, 20 international organisations, and 600,000 attendees. The summit's headline achievement: 91 countries and international organisations signed the New Delhi AI Declaration — shifting the global AI governance conversation from the 'risk' framing established in Bletchley and Paris to a new 'impact' framing focused on People, Planet, and Progress. India also set a Guinness World Record for the most pledges for an AI responsibility campaign in 24 hours: 250,946 participants. This positions India not just as an AI builder but as the country that is defining the ethical and policy framework for AI in the Global South.

video:video.video:title: AI Hiring in India Surges 32% — But 84% of Workers Feel Unprepared for AI-Driven Jobs
video:video.video:description: AI-linked job postings in India are growing at 32 percent year-on-year in 2026, heading toward 380,000 open AI roles. AI skills now appear in 14 percent of all Indian job listings — up from 12.8 percent just three months ago. Bengaluru leads with 26 percent of all AI roles, but Hyderabad is growing fastest among Tier 1 cities, and Jaipur, Indore, and Mysuru are emerging as Tier 2 hotspots. The catch: 84 percent of Indian professionals say they feel unprepared to compete in this market, and for advanced roles like Generative AI Engineer, there may be as few as one qualified candidate for every ten open positions. The demand is real. The readiness is not.

video:video.video:title: India to Quintuple Its GPU Capacity to 100,000 by End of 2026 — L&T and Yotta Lead the Build
video:video.video:description: India is executing one of the fastest sovereign AI infrastructure builds in the world. The country already has 38,000 GPUs deployed and has announced plans to expand to 100,000 by end of 2026 — a near-tripling in less than a year. Larsen & Toubro is building gigawatt-scale NVIDIA AI factories in Chennai and Mumbai. Yotta Data Services is constructing a $2 billion AI hub called Shakti Cloud powered by over 20,000 NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs. Companies at the India AI Summit committed $277 billion in investment over five to seven years. For any Indian developer, researcher, or startup that could not afford compute, access is about to get fundamentally easier.

video:video.video:title: Sarvam AI Hits $1.5 Billion Valuation — Its 105B-Parameter Model Now Rivals Global Giants
video:video.video:description: Sarvam AI, India's sovereign AI startup founded in Bengaluru in 2023, is closing a $350 million funding round at a $1.5 billion valuation — making it one of the most valuable AI companies ever built in India. At the India AI Impact Summit in February 2026, Sarvam unveiled two large language models: Sarvam-30B and the flagship Sarvam-105B, a 105-billion parameter mixture-of-experts model with a 128,000-token context window capable of complex reasoning and enterprise tasks. Both models are optimised for Indian languages, edge deployment, and data sovereignty. India is no longer just consuming global AI — it is building frontier models that compete at the top of global benchmarks.

video:video.video:title: Meta acquires humanoid robotics startup Assured Robot Intelligence to accelerate embodied AI ambitio
video:video.video:description: Meta has acquired Assured Robot Intelligence, a humanoid robotics startup, to strengthen its AI models for physical robots as the company pushes deeper into embodied AI research. The acquisition signals Meta's intention to compete with Tesla, Figure, and other players racing to build robots that can operate in human environments using AI. Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed, but the move reflects the broader industry conviction that the next frontier of AI is physical, not just digital.

video:video.video:title: Behind China's AI boom: rural workers in data-labelling rooms are the hidden human layer powering mo
video:video.video:description: A Sixth Tone investigation reveals that in China's less-developed inland provinces, labelling training data for AI models has become a government-backed poverty-alleviation strategy, with rural workers earning wages by annotating images, text, and audio in repurposed computer rooms. The work is repetitive, low-paid, and largely invisible to the consumers and companies that benefit from the resulting AI systems. The piece raises questions about who bears the human cost of AI advancement and whether data-labelling work offers a genuine pathway out of poverty or a temporary stopgap.

video:video.video:title: UK's NCSC warns AI-powered bug hunting will unleash a patch tsunami of long-buried code vulnerabilit
video:video.video:description: Britain's National Cyber Security Centre has issued a warning that AI-assisted vulnerability discovery is rapidly surfacing decades of previously undetected software flaws, creating a wave of urgent patches that security teams will struggle to absorb. The agency says years of accumulated technical debt in codebases — shortcuts and legacy decisions made by developers under time pressure — are now being exposed at machine speed. Organisations are advised to prioritise patch management infrastructure and incident response capacity before the volume of disclosures overwhelms them.

video:video.video:title: Musk v. Altman week one: xAI distils OpenAI models, Musk claims he was duped into funding the compan
video:video.video:description: In the first week of the landmark civil trial between Elon Musk and OpenAI, Musk testified that CEO Sam Altman and president Greg Brockman deceived him into financing the company, and warned the court that AI poses an existential threat to humanity. Most significantly, Musk admitted under questioning that his own AI company xAI has been distilling — training derivative models from — OpenAI's outputs, a practice that raises its own legal and ethical questions. The trial, which centres on OpenAI's conversion from a nonprofit to a for-profit entity, is expected to continue for several weeks with more witnesses.

video:video.video:title: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences bans AI-generated actors and scripts from Oscar eligibil
video:video.video:description: The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences has formally ruled that films featuring AI-generated actors or AI-written scripts are ineligible for Oscar consideration. The decision sets a clear cultural and industry line on the role of AI in Hollywood storytelling and comes amid growing anxiety among actors, writers, and directors about automation displacing human creative labour. The ruling is expected to influence eligibility standards at other major film festivals and awards bodies worldwide.

video:video.video:title: AI helped Shenzhen judges handle 50% more cases in 2025 and will now expand to dozens of Chinese cit
video:video.video:description: Judges at Shenzhen's Intermediate People's Court processed 50 percent more cases in 2025 compared to 2024, with each judge handling an average of 744 cases — up by 249 — after deploying a pilot AI-powered case management system. The court has announced the system will now be rolled out to dozens of additional Chinese cities. The development marks one of the most concrete large-scale deployments of AI in a national judicial system, raising both efficiency and due-process questions.

video:video.video:title: Harvard study finds AI outperformed two human doctors on emergency room diagnoses
video:video.video:description: A new Harvard University study tested large language models against real emergency room cases and found that at least one AI model was more accurate in its diagnoses than two human emergency physicians evaluated in the same scenarios. The research examined AI performance across a variety of medical contexts, not just ER diagnoses, and represents one of the most rigorous head-to-head comparisons of AI versus human clinical judgement to date. The findings are likely to intensify the debate over how and when AI should be integrated into frontline medical decision-making.

video:video.video:title: Five Eyes spy agencies warn agentic AI rollouts are too risky and urge slow, resilience-first adopti
video:video.video:description: Intelligence and cybersecurity agencies from the Five Eyes alliance — including the US CISA, UK NCSC, and counterparts from Australia, New Zealand, and Canada — have jointly published guidance warning that agentic AI systems are likely to misbehave and will amplify existing organisational security weaknesses. The agencies advise prioritising resilience over productivity gains and recommend slow, carefully staged adoption rather than rapid enterprise deployment. The guidance is the first coordinated multinational policy statement on the specific risks of autonomous AI agents acting on behalf of organisations.

video:video.video:title: Chinese court rules AI cost-cutting is not legal grounds to fire workers, setting landmark precedent
video:video.video:description: A court in Hangzhou, China has ruled that a fintech company acted illegally when it dismissed a 35-year-old employee on the grounds that an AI replacement would be cheaper, rejecting the argument that cost savings from automation justify termination. The worker, surnamed Zhou, had overseen AI-generated responses and was offered a demotion and pay cut before being fired for refusing. The ruling is being watched closely as China grapples with rising anxiety about AI-driven unemployment, and the court affirmed that existing labour protections cover workers displaced by automation.

video:video.video:title: Pentagon inks AI deals with Nvidia, Microsoft, and AWS to deploy models on classified networks
video:video.video:description: The US Department of Defense has signed new contracts with Nvidia, Microsoft, and Amazon Web Services to bring AI capabilities into classified government networks. The move comes after the DoD's high-profile dispute with Anthropic over the terms of use for its AI models, prompting the Pentagon to diversify its AI vendor base. The deals signal a major escalation in the US military's adoption of commercial AI for sensitive operations.

video:video.video:title: Vect ransomware hitting AI toolchains is actually a wiper — paying ransom recovers nothing
video:video.video:description: Check Point Research has confirmed that the Vect malware spreading through AI toolchain supply chains — including Trivy and LiteLLM — is not true ransomware but a destructive wiper that permanently destroys any file larger than 128KB, making full recovery impossible even after paying the demanded ransom. Organisations that have already paid to recover data are unlikely to retrieve it, as the attack is designed to destroy rather than encrypt. The finding is a critical warning for the growing ecosystem of companies deploying AI infrastructure that relies on open-source tooling.

video:video.video:title: IBM's AI coding assistant 'Bob' reaches global availability after 80,000-employee internal trial
video:video.video:description: IBM has announced global availability of Bob, its AI coding assistant, after a year-long internal trial involving 80,000 IBM employees who served as a test base across enterprise and mainframe development workflows. IBM reports productivity improvements from the trial but has not published specific metrics publicly. Bob's general availability makes it one of the largest enterprise AI coding tools deployed at scale, entering a market that includes GitHub Copilot and Amazon CodeWhisperer.

video:video.video:title: US lawmakers introduce bill mandating first comprehensive State Department assessment of China's AI
video:video.video:description: US lawmakers have unveiled a draft bill that would, for the first time, require the State Department to deliver a comprehensive report to Congress on China's AI development, including progress on autonomous capabilities benchmarked against international standards and identification of key Chinese AI leaders. The bill reflects escalating concern in Washington about the pace and ambition of China's AI programme following the release of DeepSeek V4 and advances by labs including Alibaba, Baidu, and ByteDance. If passed, it would formalise the US government's China AI intelligence-gathering framework.

video:video.video:title: Humanitarian AI agents deployed by IRC provide critical assistance to refugees as crises outpace cap
video:video.video:description: The International Rescue Committee has deployed purpose-built AI agents to provide information and assistance to refugees and displaced populations, as humanitarian organisations face caseloads that vastly exceed human staff capacity. The AI system is designed with a safety-first architecture, aiming to avoid the harms that general-purpose AI tools can cause in high-stakes, vulnerable-population contexts. The deployment represents one of the most significant real-world tests of AI in the humanitarian sector to date.

video:video.video:title: Lovable launches vibe-coding app on iOS and Android, bringing AI web development to mobile
video:video.video:description: Lovable has launched its AI-powered 'vibe coding' application on both iOS and Android, allowing developers and non-technical users to build web apps and websites directly from a mobile device using natural language prompts. The app extends Lovable's browser-based platform to mobile, targeting a fast-growing segment of developers who want to prototype and build on the go. The launch reflects a broader industry trend of making AI-assisted software creation accessible without traditional coding skills.

video:video.video:title: Health-care AI is proliferating in hospitals, but evidence it helps patients remains thin
video:video.video:description: AI tools are now embedded in hospital workflows across note-taking, patient record analysis, diagnostics, and triage flagging, but rigorous evidence that these systems actually improve patient outcomes remains scarce. MIT Technology Review's investigation finds that adoption is outpacing clinical validation, with many tools deployed based on efficiency gains rather than demonstrated health benefits. Experts warn that without robust outcome data, hospitals risk institutionalising AI systems that may not deliver — or could even harm — patient care.

video:video.video:title: EU orders Google to open Android's AI sandbox to rival assistants under Digital Markets Act
video:video.video:description: The European Commission is moving to require Google to open its Android AI sandbox — currently giving Gemini privileged deep-device access — to competing AI assistants under the Digital Markets Act. The measures would compel Google to grant rival services the same system-level integration it provides to its own AI, affecting billions of Android users globally. This is one of the most concrete AI competition enforcement actions taken under the DMA to date and sets a precedent for platform-level AI access rules.

video:video.video:title: DeepMind's David Silver raises $1.1B to build AI that learns without any human-generated data
video:video.video:description: Ineffable Intelligence, founded by former DeepMind researcher David Silver — the architect of AlphaGo — has raised $1.1 billion in funding at a valuation of $5.1 billion just months after its founding. The lab is pursuing a fundamentally different approach to AI, building systems that learn entirely without human-generated training data. If successful, this would remove one of the core bottlenecks in modern AI development: the requirement for vast quantities of human-labelled or human-produced content.

video:video.video:title: OpenAI and Microsoft end exclusivity: OpenAI free to sell on AWS in exchange for revenue-share deal
video:video.video:description: OpenAI has secured major concessions from its largest investor Microsoft, dissolving the exclusive cloud-hosting arrangement and allowing OpenAI to sell its products on Amazon Web Services. In return, Microsoft receives an expanded revenue-share agreement, and OpenAI models including a new agent service became available on AWS Bedrock within 24 hours of the deal being announced. The move marks a fundamental shift in the cloud AI landscape, opening OpenAI's technology to a far broader base of enterprise customers.

video:video.video:title: Elon Musk and Sam Altman head to trial over OpenAI's for-profit future and IPO plans
video:video.video:description: Elon Musk and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman are heading to trial in Northern California in a case that could determine whether OpenAI is legally permitted to operate as a for-profit company ahead of its anticipated IPO. A court ruling could potentially oust current leadership or block the corporate restructuring that underpins OpenAI's $50 billion Amazon deal and broader commercial expansion. The outcome would reshape the governance of one of the world's most consequential AI labs and set precedent for how AI nonprofits can convert to commercial entities.

video:video.video:title: Otter.ai launches cross-enterprise search connecting Gmail, Drive, Notion, Jira, and Salesforce
video:video.video:description: Otter.ai has launched a new feature allowing users to connect and query data across Gmail, Google Drive, Notion, Jira, and Salesforce alongside their existing meeting transcripts, creating a unified AI-powered search layer across enterprise tools. Microsoft Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, and Slack integrations are planned for the near future. The feature directly targets the daily productivity pain point of information being siloed across multiple platforms, a problem affecting millions of knowledge workers.

video:video.video:title: Vect ransomware hitting AI toolchains is actually a wiper — paying ransom recovers nothing
video:video.video:description: Check Point Research has confirmed that organisations hit by supply-chain attacks targeting Trivy and LiteLLM AI toolchain components — and who paid the Vect ransom — almost certainly did not recover their data, because Vect is not true ransomware but a wiper that permanently destroys any file larger than 128KB. The attacks are spreading through AI developer infrastructure that is increasingly integrated into enterprise systems worldwide. Security researchers warn that full data recovery is impossible for victims regardless of whether a ransom is paid.

video:video.video:title: Amazon adds AI-powered audio Q&A to product pages, letting shoppers ask questions by voice
video:video.video:description: Amazon has launched a new feature called 'Join the chat' that allows shoppers to ask questions about products on its platform and receive AI-powered audio responses, moving beyond text-based Q&A. The feature is part of Amazon's broader push to embed conversational AI across its retail experience, potentially reducing friction in purchase decisions for hundreds of millions of customers. It also signals a shift toward voice as a primary interface for AI-assisted shopping.

video:video.video:title: US lawmakers introduce bill mandating first comprehensive State Department assessment of China's AI
video:video.video:description: US lawmakers have unveiled a draft bill that would, for the first time, legally require the State Department to deliver a detailed assessment of China's AI development to Congress, including identifying specific Chinese AI leaders and benchmarking China's progress against independent public metrics. The bill reflects escalating concern in Washington about the pace of Chinese AI advancement and the lack of structured intelligence on the topic feeding into policymaking. If passed, the resulting report would become a key document shaping US AI export controls, investment restrictions, and diplomatic strategy toward Beijing.

video:video.video:title: Humanitarian AI agents deployed by IRC provide critical assistance to refugees as crises outpace cap
video:video.video:description: The International Rescue Committee and its Signpost project are deploying purpose-built AI agents designed with safety guardrails to provide critical information and assistance to refugees and displaced populations, as the scale of global humanitarian crises increasingly outstrips human capacity to respond. The AI agents are purpose-designed rather than general-purpose, with a focus on avoiding harm to vulnerable users. The project represents one of the more concrete real-world tests of whether AI can be responsibly deployed in high-stakes, low-resource contexts outside the Global North.

video:video.video:title: YouTube tests AI-powered guided search answers for US Premium subscribers
video:video.video:description: YouTube is rolling out a new AI-powered search feature to Premium subscribers in the United States on an opt-in basis, surfacing guided answers directly in search results rather than just video lists. The feature represents Google's push to make YouTube a destination for AI-synthesised information, not just video discovery, competing more directly with AI search tools like Perplexity and ChatGPT Search. The opt-in rollout suggests YouTube is gathering user feedback before a broader release.

video:video.video:title: IBM's AI coding assistant 'Bob' reaches global availability after 80,000-employee internal trial
video:video.video:description: IBM has announced global general availability of Bob, its AI coding assistant, following an internal pilot with 80,000 IBM employees used as test subjects over the past year. IBM claims the tool delivered measurable productivity gains, though specific metrics have not been independently verified. The launch positions IBM as a direct competitor in the crowded enterprise AI coding market alongside GitHub Copilot, Cursor, and Amazon CodeWhisperer, with the added hook of mainframe support.

video:video.video:title: EU orders Google to open Android's AI sandbox to rival assistants under Digital Markets Act
video:video.video:description: The European Commission is drawing up measures requiring Google to give competing AI assistants the same deep device-level access on Android smartphones that its own Gemini assistant currently enjoys, under Digital Markets Act enforcement. The move is aimed at preventing Google from locking rival AI services out of the most important hardware layer — the smartphone — as AI assistants become central to daily digital life. If implemented, billions of Android users globally could see more choice in which AI assistant integrates natively with their device.

video:video.video:title: Amazon launches OpenAI models on AWS Bedrock one day after Microsoft exclusivity ends
video:video.video:description: Just one day after OpenAI reached an agreement with Microsoft to end exclusive cloud rights, Amazon Web Services announced a slate of OpenAI model offerings on its Bedrock platform, including a new agent service. The rapid rollout signals how quickly the AI market is restructuring now that OpenAI can sell across multiple cloud providers. For businesses already on AWS, this means direct access to OpenAI's latest models without migrating infrastructure.

video:video.video:title: Google expands Pentagon AI contract after Anthropic refuses DoD surveillance and weapons use
video:video.video:description: Google has signed a new contract expanding the US Department of Defense's access to its AI systems, stepping in after Anthropic declined to permit the DoD to use its models for domestic mass surveillance and autonomous weapons systems. The move highlights a growing divide among AI labs over where to draw ethical lines on military and surveillance applications. It raises immediate questions about the accountability frameworks governing AI in national security contexts and what safeguards, if any, are attached to Google's agreement.

video:video.video:title: China's deaf delivery riders say gig algorithms give them fairer treatment than human employers
video:video.video:description: A Sixth Tone investigation found that deaf and hard-of-hearing workers in China are increasingly gravitating to food delivery platforms, reporting that algorithm-driven dispatch systems treat them more equitably than human managers who may discriminate based on disability. While most gig workers describe algorithmic management as oppressive, deaf couriers say the system's indifference to identity is a form of fairness they rarely encountered in traditional employment. The story highlights how AI-driven labour platforms can have uneven and sometimes counterintuitive social effects.

video:video.video:title: Chinese robot 'Lightning' beats the men's half-marathon world record in mixed human-robot race
video:video.video:description: A Chinese humanoid robot named Lightning won China's second annual mixed human-robot half-marathon, completing the course in a time that surpassed the existing men's world record for the distance. The event, which saw robots and human runners compete on the same course, is part of China's broader national push to develop competitive humanoid robotics. The result is being cited by Chinese researchers as a milestone in bipedal locomotion and real-world robot endurance.

video:video.video:title: AI is accelerating the global e-waste crisis as hardware demand surges and waste flows to poorer nat
video:video.video:description: Rest of World reports that the rapid expansion of AI hardware infrastructure is dramatically worsening the global e-waste problem, with discarded GPUs, servers, and consumer AI devices disproportionately ending up in informal recycling operations in non-Western countries. The piece documents how existing e-waste trade routes and processing capacity in Africa, South and Southeast Asia are being overwhelmed by the accelerating hardware replacement cycles driven by AI model upgrades. Inadequate regulatory oversight in receiving countries means workers face health risks from toxic materials with little protection. The article calls for AI hardware manufacturers and hyperscalers to take extended producer responsibility for end-of-life equipment.

video:video.video:title: ComfyUI raises $30M at $500M valuation as creators demand more control over AI-generated media
video:video.video:description: ComfyUI, a platform that gives creators granular control over AI-generated image, video, and audio output, has raised $30 million in new funding at a $500 million valuation. The round signals growing investor conviction that professional and semi-professional creators want fine-grained tools rather than fully automated black-box AI generators. ComfyUI's node-based workflow system has attracted a large open-source community before this funding round. The company plans to use the capital to expand its tooling and enterprise offering.

video:video.video:title: Deadly deepfakes in conflict zones: AI-generated disinformation is putting civilians at risk globall
video:video.video:description: Researcher Rachel Adams, writing for Rest of World, documents how AI-generated deepfakes are being deployed as weapons of disinformation in active conflict zones, directly undermining civilian safety by spreading false evacuation orders, fabricated atrocity footage, and fake official communications. The analysis highlights that the burden of AI-generated disinformation falls disproportionately on populations in the Global South, where platform moderation and AI detection tools are weakest. Adams calls out the role of Western technology companies in providing the infrastructure that enables this harm without adequate safeguards for non-Western users. The piece is an analytical essay rather than a breaking news report, drawing on documented cases from multiple conflict regions.

video:video.video:title: Netflix's AI deal with Ben Affleck's startup threatens VFX jobs across India, South Korea, and Latin
video:video.video:description: Netflix has acquired Interpositive, a VFX startup co-founded by actor Ben Affleck, whose AI technology automates the frame-by-frame visual effects work that is currently performed by large workforces of artists in India, South Korea, and Latin America. Rest of World reports that the deal could displace significant numbers of workers in countries where Hollywood studios have long outsourced labour-intensive post-production tasks at lower cost. The acquisition raises concerns not only about job losses but also about the cultural and creative autonomy of non-English-speaking VFX industries. No workforce impact figures have been officially confirmed by Netflix or Interpositive.

video:video.video:title: Cohere merges with Aleph Alpha to build sovereign AI alternative for European enterprises
video:video.video:description: Canadian AI startup Cohere is acquiring Germany-based Aleph Alpha in a deal backed by Schwarz Group, the parent company of European retailer Lidl, with the explicit goal of offering a sovereign AI alternative to US-dominated providers for European enterprises. Both governments have signalled support for the transaction, framing it as a strategic move to reduce dependence on American AI infrastructure. The combined entity is expected to serve large enterprises seeking data sovereignty and compliance with EU AI and data regulations. Financial terms of the deal have not been fully disclosed.

video:video.video:title: Health-care AI is proliferating in hospitals, but evidence it helps patients remains thin
video:video.video:description: AI tools are now widely used across US hospitals for clinical notetaking, patient record triage, flagging at-risk individuals, and interpreting X-rays and medical exam results. Despite this rapid deployment, MIT Technology Review reports that robust clinical evidence demonstrating these tools actually improve patient outcomes remains scarce. Hospitals are adopting AI faster than the research community can evaluate it, raising questions about whether procurement decisions are driven by efficiency promises rather than proven benefit. The article calls for more rigorous, independent trials before broader mandated rollout.

video:video.video:title: AI optimism surges across Asia while Americans remain sceptical and distrust regulators
video:video.video:description: New research published by Rest of World shows a striking divergence in public attitudes toward AI: populations across Asia express significantly higher optimism about AI's benefits compared to Americans, who also report far lower trust in regulators to govern the technology responsibly. The findings suggest that cultural, economic, and governance contexts shape how societies receive and adopt AI, with potential long-term implications for where AI investment and talent flows. The survey did not specify which Asian countries were included or the sample sizes involved. These attitudinal gaps could influence how governments design AI policy and how companies prioritise regional market strategies.

video:video.video:title: DeepSeek V4 preview released: longer context, open weights, and Huawei NPU support
video:video.video:description: Chinese AI firm DeepSeek has released a preview of V4, its new flagship large language model, featuring significantly extended context windows enabled by a new architectural design for handling large amounts of text efficiently. Like its predecessors, V4 is open source and freely available, and it adds expanded support for Huawei's Ascend AI accelerator chips, reducing dependence on Nvidia hardware. MIT Technology Review identified three key reasons the model matters: its performance targets top proprietary models, its inference costs are a fraction of comparable systems, and its open-weights availability could shift global AI development dynamics. The model's preview status means full benchmarks have not yet been independently validated.

video:video.video:title: Anthropic runs agent-on-agent commerce experiment where AI buys and sells real goods
video:video.video:description: Anthropic designed a classified-ad marketplace in which AI agents acted as both buyers and sellers, negotiating and completing transactions for real goods with real money. The experiment is among the first documented cases of fully autonomous agent-to-agent commerce at a reputable AI lab. The findings could inform how future AI systems handle procurement, supply chains, and consumer purchasing on behalf of humans. Anthropic has not yet disclosed the full scope of goods exchanged or the total monetary value of transactions.

video:video.video:title: Google commits up to $40B investment in Anthropic for cash and compute capacity
video:video.video:description: Google has announced plans to invest up to $40 billion in AI safety company Anthropic, combining cash and compute resources in what would be one of the largest AI sector deals on record. The investment follows Anthropic's limited release of Mythos, a powerful model focused on cybersecurity applications. The deal signals that leading tech firms are racing to lock in massive infrastructure advantages as competition in frontier AI intensifies. This level of compute backing could directly shape which AI tools reach consumers and enterprises over the next several years.
